issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Pneumatic.raisePressure(pressureIncrease: double) (problem_statement.md lines 16-19) but elsewhere in the problem text the method is referred to as raisePressure(int pressureIncrease) (problem_statement.md line 71) and the solution implements raisePressure(int pressureIncrease) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java). This creates a direct signature mismatch: students reading the UML may implement a double parameter, while the solution and textual remark use int. This ambiguity will confuse students about the correct method signature and can cause test/signature mismatches.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the parameter type for raisePressure consistent across all artifacts. Either: (a) change the UML and any textual references in problem_statement.md to use int (raisePressure(int pressureIncrease)) to match the current solution and implementations; or (b) change the solution (and Launched* implementations) to use double and update the Pneumatic interface accordingly. Recommended quick fix: update the UML/text to use int and ensure the template Pneumatic.java declares void raisePressure(int pressureIncrease); so students have an unambiguous signature to implement.
